summary: 'Ichthyol Pale' refers to pale (light) sulfonated shale oil, a refined, lighter-coloured and less malodorous form of ichthammol used in dermatology. Applied topically (typically as a cream or ointment in low percentage), it has anti-inflammatory, mild antibacterial, antiseborrhoeic and antipruritic actions and is used for mild inflammatory and seborrhoeic skin conditions, eczema/dermatitis, and as a drawing agent for superficial boils/folliculitis. The pale grade is preferred cosmetically because it stains less and has little odour compared with dark ichthammol. It is a long-established dermatological preparation described in European monographs/SmPCs rather than as a modern FDA prescription label; use is supported by traditional/established dermatological practice.

moa: Sulfonated shale oil (ichthammol) is obtained by distillation and sulfonation of bituminous (oil) shale rich in fossilised marine organic matter. Its sulfur-containing organic constituents exert local anti-inflammatory effects (inhibition of inflammatory mediators such as leukotrienes/lipoxygenase activity), mild antibacterial and antimycotic activity, antiseborrhoeic action by reducing sebaceous activity, and an antipruritic/keratoplastic effect. The pale grade is a purified, lighter fraction with the same general actions but reduced colour and odour.

missed: If you miss an application, apply it when you remember; if it is almost time for the next, skip the missed one and continue as usual. Do not double up.
overdose: Topical overdose is very unlikely to cause systemic harm; excessive application may cause local irritation. Wipe off excess and treat any skin irritation supportively. Accidental ingestion should be managed symptomatically with medical advice.
